fields.reasoning: The question's evidence checks out in the code: repoFreeBytes (internal/api/daemon.go) honours RHIZA_TEST_FREE_BYTES only through ctxGetenv(ctx) alongside RHIZA_TEST_NOW and otherwise calls daemon.FreeBytes(ctx.Root); cmd/rhiza/main_test.go pins testFreeBytes = 1 TiB for scripts, but the internal/api tests build Ctx values without that Getenv, so they read the runner's real disk. A runner at 3.7 GiB free trips the 10 GiB guard, the daemon holds schedule starts and the health disk part goes bad, which is exactly the three failing tests; attempt 2 at the same commit passed, and #379's next head passed, which a real merge interaction would not do. ci.yml already dispatches CI for a main commit whose tree differs from the tested head, and ship merge requires the head to contain origin/main, so main's tree was the tested tree. Building a merge queue or post-merge red-main pause would add machinery against a failure that did not happen and leave the actual flake in place; fixing the test hermeticity removes the cause and stays inside the change set's purpose (main and PRs going red for no real defect).
fields.statement: This change set builds no merge gate, merge queue or post-merge CI on main. It makes the internal/api Go tests hermetic about free disk: every test that reaches repoFreeBytes (the daemon's disk guard and health's disk part, via the schedule and health tests) gets a pinned free-disk figure, the same 1 TiB the cmd/rhiza scripts pin with RHIZA_TEST_FREE_BYTES, through the Ctx's Getenv (or one shared test helper that builds such a Ctx), so no internal/api test reads the CI host's real free space. A test that wants low disk sets the figure itself. Acceptance: with the host's free space below 10 GiB (simulated by making daemon.FreeBytes unreachable from the tests, e.g. a test that fails if the real figure is consulted), TestDaemonPollStartsEachProjectsSchedule, TestDaemonScheduleUnresolvedWorkflow and TestHealthSchedulesPart still pass. The change set's intent should be narrowed to this flaky-test fix.
